overview: This 171-page file traces the dispute over foreign perpetual leaseholds in Japan from tax demands and property surveys to the 1937 diplomatic settlements. American, British, and Japanese correspondence documents competing proposals, negotiations, and agreements to convert leaseholds to ownership in April 1942 while preserving tax protections until then. It also includes French and Italian agreements, local tax regulations, and reports on Japanese settlement and migration.
interest: Property inventories and successive draft notes reveal how local tax disputes became coordinated international settlements.
